subproblem.title: Blow-up integrals of compactly supported functions: eventual localization to an open neighbourhood, and eventual vanishing at a null ball (parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For a measure ν on ℝ^P, a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0, write ν^{a,s} := ofReal(s^{−n})•ν.map(dilation a s), where dilation a s (y) = s⁻¹(y − a). Let λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ) with λ_j → 0, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ have compact support. No continuity or integrability of f is assumed; integrals are Bochner integrals. (a) If μ is a measure on ℝ^P, G ⊆ ℝ^P is open and p ∈ G, then ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,λ_j} = ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} for all sufficiently large j. (b) If μ is a measure on ℝ^P, p ∈ ℝ^P, ε > 0 and μ(B_ε(p)) = 0, then ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} = 0 for all sufficiently large j.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (p : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen G → p ∈ G → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → HasCompactSupport f → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) • (μ.restrict G).map (dilation p (lams j))) = ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) • μ.map (dilation p (lams j)))) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (p : Euclid P) (ε : ℝ) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), 0 < ε → μ (ball p ε) = 0 → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → HasCompactSupport f → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) • μ.map (dilation p (lams j))) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (localization: (μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η_{p,s}(G) ⊇ B_{δ/s}(0), and tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/λ_j}(0) for large j) and step 2 (a null ball B_ε(p) makes the blow-up integrals eventually 0). The parent proof takes these dilation facts from its sibling ambient_calculus (items (2), (3), (4), (9)); they are proved directly here.
Notation: for a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0, η := dilation a s, so η(y) = −s⁻¹a + s⁻¹y = s⁻¹(y − a). Write c_s := ofReal((s)⁻¹ ^ n).
1. (η is a homeomorphism.) For s ≠ 0, η is the composition of y ↦ s⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero) and z ↦ −s⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft). Hence η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P and so a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding); in particular it is injective and measurable. It is surjective: η(a + s z) = z for every z.
2. (Balls.) Let s > 0. Then η(y) = s⁻¹(y − a), so ‖η(y)‖ = |s⁻¹|·‖y − a‖ = ‖y − a‖/s. Hence, for every r ∈ ℝ, η⁻¹(B_r(0)) = {y : ‖y − a‖/s < r} = {y : ‖y − a‖ < s r} = B_{s r}(a). Since η is surjective, B_r(0) = η(η⁻¹(B_r(0))) = η(B_{s r}(a)). With r = δ/s this gives B_{δ/s}(0) = η(B_δ(a)) for every δ, since s·(δ/s) = δ.
3. (Eventual containment of the support.) Let r > 0. Since tsupport f is compact, it is bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 M for some M ∈ ℝ. Since λ_j > 0 for all j and λ_j → 0, λ_j → 0 within (0, ∞) (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Hence λ_j⁻¹ → +∞ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero), and r/λ_j = r·λ_j⁻¹ → +∞ (Tendsto.const_mul_atTop, r > 0). So r/λ_j > M for all large j, and then tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 M ⊆ B_{r/λ_j}(0) (closedBall_subset_ball).
4. (Proof of (a).) G is open and p ∈ G, so there is δ > 0 with B_δ(p) ⊆ G (Metric.isOpen_iff). By step 3 with r := δ, tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/λ_j}(0) for all large j. Fix such a j and put s := λ_j > 0 and η := dilation p s.
 (i) (Restriction commutes with the blow-up.) Since η is a measurable embedding, (μ.map η)⌞η(G) = (μ⌞η⁻¹(η(G))).map η (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map), and η⁻¹(η(G)) = G by injectivity (preimage_image_eq). Multiply by the scalar c_s and use (c•ν)⌞B = c•(ν⌞B) (Measure.restrict_smul). This gives c_s•(μ⌞G).map η = (c_s•μ.map η)⌞η(G), i.e. (μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η(G). Hence ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,s} = ∫_{η(G)} f dμ^{p,s}.
 (ii) (f vanishes off η(G).) Let x ∉ η(G) and suppose f(x) ≠ 0. Then x ∈ support f ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/s}(0). By step 2 with a := p, B_{δ/s}(0) = η(B_δ(p)) ⊆ η(G), because B_δ(p) ⊆ G. This contradicts x ∉ η(G). So f(x) = 0 for every x ∉ η(G).
 (iii) By (ii), ∫_{η(G)} f dμ^{p,s} = ∫ f dμ^{p,s} (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, which needs no measurability or integrability hypothesis). With (i), ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,λ_j} = ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} for all large j, which is (a).
5. (Proof of (b).) By step 3 with r := ε, tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/λ_j}(0) for all large j. Fix such j and put s := λ_j > 0 and η := dilation p s.
 (i) (The ball is null.) B_{ε/s}(0) is measurable and η is measurable. So μ^{p,s}(B_{ε/s}(0)) = c_s·(μ.map η)(B_{ε/s}(0)) = c_s·μ(η⁻¹(B_{ε/s}(0))) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply). By step 2 this equals c_s·μ(B_{s·(ε/s)}(p)) = c_s·μ(B_ε(p)) = c_s·0 = 0.
 (ii) {x : f(x) ≠ 0} = support f ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/s}(0), so this set is μ^{p,s}-null (measure_mono_null). That is, f = 0 μ^{p,s}-almost everywhere (ae_iff). Hence ∫ f dμ^{p,s} = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
 This holds for all large j, which is (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation a s (s > 0) is a surjective homeomorphism (a measurable embedding) with η⁻¹(B_r(0)) = B_{sr}(a) and η(B_δ(a)) = B_{δ/s}(0).
tsupport f is bounded and r/λ_j → +∞, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{r/λ_j}(0) for all large j.
(μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η(G) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, Measure.restrict_smul). For large j, f vanishes off η(G) ⊇ η(B_δ(p)) = B_{δ/s}(0), so the two integrals agree.
μ^{p,s}(B_{ε/s}(0)) = ofReal(s^{−n})·μ(B_ε(p)) = 0, so for large j, f = 0 μ^{p,s}-a.e. and ∫ f dμ^{p,s} = 0.

subproblem.title: Degree-n homogeneous measures have scale-invariant upper density ratios: limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(t·w, ρ) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(w, ρ) (parent step 6, (F5))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let ν be a measure on ℝ^P such that ν((v ↦ λv)(A)) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A) for every λ > 0 and every measurable A ⊆ ℝ^P. For w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, let r_ν(w, ρ) := ν(B_ρ(w))/(unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Then for every t > 0 and every w ∈ ℝ^P, limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(t·w, ρ) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(w, ρ), with both limsups taken in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>]0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν ((fun x => lam • x) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) * ν A) → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ w : Euclid P, limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (ball (t • w) ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) = limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (ball w ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 6 (homogeneous density of the tangent cone weight, (F5)). It is stated here for any measure with the degree-n homogeneity that the sibling cone_measure_homogeneous (Submission.cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image) provides for the weight of a cone.
Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ [0, ∞]; no finiteness or positivity of ω_n is used. Write h(ρ) := r_ν(w, ρ) = ν(B_ρ(w))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)).
1. (Scaled balls.) Fix t > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, and let ρ > 0. By smul_ball (t ≠ 0), t•B_{ρ/t}(w) = B_{‖t‖·(ρ/t)}(t•w) = B_ρ(t•w), since ‖t‖ = |t| = t and t·(ρ/t) = ρ. Also t•B = (v ↦ t v)''B (Set.image_smul). So B_ρ(t w) = (v ↦ t v)''B_{ρ/t}(w).
2. (Numerator.) Balls are measurable, so the hypothesis with λ := t and A := B_{ρ/t}(w) gives ν(B_ρ(t w)) = ofReal(t^n)·ν(B_{ρ/t}(w)).
3. (Denominator.) ρ^n = (t·(ρ/t))^n = t^n·(ρ/t)^n (mul_pow). Since t^n ≥ 0, ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(t^n)·ofReal((ρ/t)^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(t^n)·(ω_n·ofReal((ρ/t)^n)), using commutativity and associativity in [0, ∞].
4. (Cancellation.) c := ofReal(t^n) satisfies c ≠ 0 (t^n > 0, ENNReal.ofReal_pos) and c ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top). By ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left, r_ν(t w, ρ) = (c·ν(B_{ρ/t}(w)))/(c·(ω_n·ofReal((ρ/t)^n))) = ν(B_{ρ/t}(w))/(ω_n·ofReal((ρ/t)^n)) = h(ρ/t). This holds for every ρ > 0.
5. (Eventual equality.) The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>]0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). So by step 4, ρ ↦ r_ν(t w, ρ) and h ∘ (ρ ↦ ρ/t) agree eventually along 𝓝[>]0 and have the same limsup there (Filter.limsup_congr).
6. (Change of variables.) limsup_{𝓝[>]0} (h ∘ (·/t)) = limsup_{map (·/t) 𝓝[>]0} h (Filter.limsup_comp).
7. (The substitution preserves 𝓝[>]0.) The maps ρ ↦ ρ/t and ρ ↦ tρ are mutually inverse (t ≠ 0). So map (·/t) F = comap (t·) F for every filter F on ℝ (Filter.map_eq_comap_of_inverse). Also comap (t·) 𝓝[>]0 = 𝓝[>]0 because t > 0 (comap_mulLeft_nhdsGT_zero). Hence map (·/t) 𝓝[>]0 = 𝓝[>]0.
8. Combining steps 5–7: limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(t w, ρ) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} h(ρ/t) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} h(ρ) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r_ν(w, ρ). ∎
proof_key_steps: B_ρ(tw) = (v ↦ tv)''B_{ρ/t}(w), so ν(B_ρ(tw)) = ofReal(t^n)·ν(B_{ρ/t}(w)), and ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(t^n)·ω_n·ofReal((ρ/t)^n).
Cancelling the finite nonzero factor ofReal(t^n) (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left) gives r_ν(tw, ρ) = r_ν(w, ρ/t) for every ρ > 0.
The limsup along 𝓝[>]0 is unchanged by the substitution ρ ↦ ρ/t: limsup_congr, limsup_comp, and map (·/t) 𝓝[>]0 = comap (t·) 𝓝[>]0 = 𝓝[>]0.

subproblem.title: The zero current of ℝ^P is a minimizing cycle with an integer multiplicity representation of zero weight (parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there exist a current C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n on Euclid P) and an integer multiplicity representation R_C of C in ℝ^P (an IMRep univ n with R_C.Represents C) such that C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), ∂C = 0 in ℝ^P (BoundaryVanishes C), and the weight of R_C is the zero measure (R_C.measure = 0). One may take C = 0 and R_C = (∅, 1, 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (RC : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsMinimizingIn C univ ∧ BoundaryVanishes C ∧ RC.Represents C ∧ RC.measure = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 (case p ∉ spt T: "Take … C := 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and R_C := the empty triple (carrier ∅, multiplicity 1, orientation 0)" and the verification that follows it); Simon 6.3.1 (integer multiplicity currents τ(M, θ, ξ)) and 7.1.1 (minimizing currents).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. For an IMRep R, R.action(ω) = ∫_{R.carrier} R.mult(x)·R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) and R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult).
1. (The current.) Let C := 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), the zero element of GeometricCurrentOn univ n. It satisfies C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply).
2. (The empty triple is an IMRep in ℝ^P.) Let R_C have carrier ∅, multiplicity the constant function 1 and orientation the constant function 0. Its fields hold:
 (a) ∅ is measurable (MeasurableSet.empty) and ∅ ⊆ univ;
 (b) ∅ is countably n-rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, since Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (measure_empty);
 (c) the constant multiplicity is measurable (measurable_const), and positivity on the carrier is vacuous because the carrier is empty;
 (d) for every compact K ⊆ univ, ∫⁻_{∅ ∩ K} 1 dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞, because ∅ ∩ K = ∅ and the restriction of a measure to ∅ is the zero measure;
 (e) Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty). So the orientation is a.e. strongly measurable for it (aestronglyMeasurable_zero_measure). The a.e. orientation condition holds because the almost-everywhere filter of the zero measure is ⊥ (ae_zero), so every property holds a.e.
3. (R_C represents C.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), R_C.action(ω) is an integral over the zero measure Hⁿ⌞∅, hence equals 0 (integral_zero_measure). By step 1, C(ω) = 0. Thus C(ω) = R_C.action(ω) for all ω, i.e. R_C.Represents C.
4. (Zero weight.) R_C.measure = (Hⁿ⌞∅).withDensity(1) = (0).withDensity(1) = 0. Indeed, every set has withDensity-measure ∫⁻ over the zero measure, which is 0.
5. (Minimality.)
 (a) C is integer multiplicity, witnessed by R_C (step 3).
 (b) For every W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(C) = sSup{ofReal(C(ω)) : ω admissible for W}, and every element of this set is ofReal(0) = 0. So M_W(C) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), hence M_W(C) = 0.
 Therefore, for every open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P and every competitor S (whatever further properties IsMinimizingIn imposes on S), M_W(C) = 0 ≤ M_W(S). Hence IsMinimizingIn C univ.
6. (Cycle.) If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes C is True by definition. If n = m + 1, BoundaryVanishes C means ∂C = 0. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), (∂C)(ω) = C(dω) = 0 = 0(ω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), so ∂C = 0 by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.
7. Steps 1–6 show that C := 0 and R_C := (∅, 1, 0) satisfy IsMinimizingIn C univ, BoundaryVanishes C, R_C.Represents C and R_C.measure = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take C = 0 and R_C = (∅, 1, 0). All IMRep conditions hold because Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, and ∅ is rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero.
R_C.action(ω) = 0 = C(ω), so R_C represents C, and R_C.measure = (0).withDensity 1 = 0.
M_W(0) is the supremum of zeros, so M_W(0) = 0 ≤ M_W(S); with C integer multiplicity, C is minimizing in ℝ^P.
∂0 = 0: trivial in degree 0; in degree m + 1, (∂0)(ω) = 0(dω) = 0.

subproblem.title: Tangent cones at points of spt T via (DTC): blow-ups of a minimizing cycle subconverge to a minimizing cone cycle, and the rescaled weights converge vaguely (parent steps 3–5, (F7))
subproblem.statement: Assume (DTC), the contract proposition DensityAndTangentCones (Simon 7.3.1). Let n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1. Let U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k}, with U open and N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Let R be an IMRep of T in U with weight μ := R.measure, let p ∈ spt T, and let λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ) with λ_j → 0. Then there exist a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ, a current C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) and an IMRep R_C of C in ℝ^{n+k} such that: C is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}; ∂C = 0; C is a cone (IsConeCurrent C); R_C represents C; and for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ, ∫ f d(ofReal(λ_{sub(j)}^{−n})•μ.map(dilation p λ_{sub(j)})) → ∫ f dR_C.measure as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: DensityAndTangentCones → ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (p : Euclid (n + k)) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N) → T.support ⊆ U ∩ N → BoundaryVanishes T → R.Represents T → p ∈ T.support → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ (sub : ℕ → ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + k))) n) (RC : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid (n + k))) n), StrictMono sub ∧ IsMinimizingIn C univ ∧ BoundaryVanishes C ∧ IsConeCurrent C ∧ RC.Represents C ∧ ∀ f : Euclid (n + k) → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams (sub j))⁻¹ ^ n) • R.measure.map (dilation p (lams (sub j))))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂RC.measure))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 3 (apply (DTC)(2) at p ∈ spt T, using spt ∂T = ∅), 4 (∂C = 0 by (F7)) and 5 (the weights converge); Simon 7.3.1(2) (statement chapter-07.txt lines 302–310, proof from line 326) and 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), (8) (lines 454–466).
Notation: P := n + k; μ := R.measure; η_{a,s} := dilation a s; λ'_j := λ_{φ(j)} once φ is chosen.
1. (p ∈ U.) spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion T ⊆ U (GeometricCurrentOn.support_subset_domain), so p ∈ U.
2. (spt ∂T = ∅.) Since n ≥ 1, write n = m + 1. By definition boundarySupport T = spt(∂T), and ∂T = 0 because BoundaryVanishes T. We show that the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_m(U) has empty support. Let q ∈ U. As U is open, choose ε > 0 with B_ε(q) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff), and put W := B_{ε/2}(q).
 - W is open and contains q.
 - closure W ⊆ closedBall q (ε/2) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), which is compact (isCompact_closedBall). So closure W is compact, being a closed subset of a compact set.
 - closure W ⊆ closedBall q (ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(q) ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball, ε/2 < ε).
 - The zero current vanishes on W, since 0(ω) = 0 for every ω.
 Hence W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion 0, so q ∈ zeroRegion 0 and q ∉ spt 0 = U ∖ zeroRegion 0. Therefore boundarySupport T = ∅ and p ∈ spt T ∖ boundarySupport T.
3. (Apply (DTC)(2).) The hypotheses of (DTC) for n, k, ℓ, U, N, T are among ours: ℓ ≤ k, U open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T minimizing in U ∩ N and spt T ⊆ U ∩ N. Apply part (2) of (DTC) at x := p ∈ spt T ∖ boundarySupport T (step 2), with the sequence (λ_j), the positivity proofs λ_j > 0, and λ_j → 0. It gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with:
 (a) ConvergesWeakly (j ↦ blowUp T p λ'_j) C;
 (b) MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp T p λ'_j) C;
 (c) IsMinimizingIn C univ;
 (d) IsConeCurrent C.
 The density statement of (DTC)(2) is not needed. Put sub := φ.
4. (∂C = 0.) Since φ is strictly increasing, φ(j) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), so λ'_j = λ_{φ(j)} → 0 (Tendsto.comp), and λ'_j > 0. Apply the sibling blowup_limit_cycle (Submission.idtp_tpf_blowUp_limit_boundaryVanishes) to P, n, U, T, x := p, the sequence (λ'_j) with the positivity proofs (j ↦ λ_{φ(j)} > 0), and the current C. Its hypotheses are: U open, p ∈ U (step 1), BoundaryVanishes T, λ'_j → 0, and the weak convergence (a). It gives BoundaryVanishes C.
5. (R_C.) By (c), C is integer multiplicity (the first component of IsMinimizingIn C univ). Fix an IMRep R_C of C in univ with R_C.Represents C.
6. (IMReps of the blow-ups.) Fix j. Apply the sibling blowup_scaling (Submission.dtc_blowUp_scaling) to P, n, U, A := U, T, x := p, λ := λ'_j > 0, U open and 0 < n (n ≥ 1). Its part (2), applied to R (which represents T), gives an IMRep R_j of blowUp T p λ'_j in η_{p,λ'_j}(U) such that R_j.measure(s) = ofReal(λ'_j^{−n})·μ(η_{p,λ'_j}⁻¹(s)) for every measurable s ⊆ ℝ^P. Choose such an R_j for every j (axiom of choice). Then R_j represents blowUp T p λ'_j for every j.
7. (Identification of the weights.) η_{p,s} : y ↦ −s⁻¹p + dilationCLM P s (y) is a constant plus a continuous linear map, so it is continuous and hence measurable. For measurable s ⊆ ℝ^P, (ofReal(λ'_j^{−n})•μ.map η_{p,λ'_j})(s) = ofReal(λ'_j^{−n})·μ(η_{p,λ'_j}⁻¹(s)) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply). So R_j.measure and ofReal(λ'_j^{−n})•μ.map(η_{p,λ'_j}) agree on all measurable sets, hence are equal (Measure.ext).
8. (Vague convergence.) Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support; trivially tsupport f ⊆ univ. Apply (b) to the family (R_j) (with R_j representing blowUp T p λ'_j), to R_C (representing C) and to f. This gives ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dR_C.measure. By step 7, this says ∫ f d(ofReal(λ_{sub(j)}^{−n})•μ.map(dilation p λ_{sub(j)})) → ∫ f dR_C.measure.
9. Thus sub = φ, C and R_C satisfy: StrictMono sub (step 3), IsMinimizingIn C univ ((c)), BoundaryVanishes C (step 4), IsConeCurrent C ((d)), R_C.Represents C (step 5), and the convergence of step 8. ∎
proof_key_steps: p ∈ spt T ⊆ U. Since n ≥ 1 and ∂T = 0, spt ∂T = spt 0 = ∅: every q ∈ U lies in an open ball W ⊂⊂ U on which 0 vanishes. So p ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T.
(DTC)(2) at p gives a strictly increasing φ and a minimizing cone C, with weak convergence and MassMeasuresConverge of the blow-ups blowUp T p λ_{φ(j)}.
blowup_limit_cycle (F7) along λ_{φ(j)} → 0 gives ∂C = 0. C is integer multiplicity, so fix an IMRep R_C.

blowup_scaling (2) gives IMReps R_j of the blow-ups with R_j.measure = ofReal(λ_{φ(j)}^{−n})•μ.map(dilation p λ_{φ(j)}) (Measure.ext, Measure.map_apply). MassMeasuresConverge then gives the vague convergence to R_C.measure.

audit.reason: All hypotheses appear in the prose and type; p ∈ U follows from p ∈ support T. Relatively compact balls justify empty boundary support. DTC supplies the subsequence and cone; the two declared dependencies establish its vanishing boundary and identify the rescaled weights. MassMeasuresConverge then gives precisely the stated convergence. DTC is used only as an explicit hypothesis.
